- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.2) after a spike, model should not continue upward; cap forecast at prior peak or adjust downward 3–5% to reflect cooling sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizons, if recent 5–7 day mean is rising, model should not overpredict beyond 1–2% above that mean unless sentiment confirms strong momentum.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.2–0.6), model should not assume trend continuation; apply mean reversion bias toward 3–5 day moving average.  
- If forecast spikes >10% above recent 10-day high, reduce by 10–15% if sentiment is weak or mixed; this prevents overconfidence in short-term momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply downward bias of 2–4% for next 30d if sentiment remains flat or negative.  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is flat or declining, model should not ignore sentiment — adjust upward 2–5% to reflect underlying bullish sentiment.
